notable_figures.name: Apo Whang-od
notable_figures.contributions: Last mambabatok (traditional Kalinga tattoo artist) preserving ancient Filipino tattoo traditions. Recipient of the 1st Hiyas Award for Indigenous Art in 2022.
notable_figures.influence: Symbol of cultural preservation and indigenous artistry, bringing international attention to traditional Filipino tattooing methods.

notable_figures.name: Sailor Jerry (Norman Keith Collins)
notable_figures.contributions: Popularized the American traditional style characterized by bold outlines and vibrant colors. His Honolulu shop in the 1950s became legendary.
notable_figures.influence: His style continues to influence modern tattooing, with his designs still being referenced and adapted by contemporary artists.

notable_figures.name: Horiyoshi III
notable_figures.contributions: Master of full-body suits and traditional Japanese motifs, maintaining and modernizing ancient techniques.
notable_figures.influence: Considered one of the greatest living masters of traditional Japanese tattooing, influencing artists worldwide.

notable_figures.name: Don Ed Hardy
notable_figures.contributions: Studied Japanese tattooing and incorporated traditional Japanese aesthetics into Western tattooing.
notable_figures.influence: Known as the 'Godfather of Modern Tattoo,' significantly influencing contemporary tattoo styles globally.

notable_figures.name: Kat Von D
notable_figures.specialty: Black and gray portraits, floral designs
notable_figures.contributions: Gained fame through TV shows Miami Ink and LA Ink, bringing tattoo artistry to mainstream media.
notable_figures.influence: Helped popularize tattooing in mainstream culture and expanded into the beauty industry.

notable_figures.name: Bang Bang (Keith McCurdy)
notable_figures.contributions: Tattooed high-profile clients like Rihanna, Justin Bieber, and Miley Cyrus.
notable_figures.influence: Called 'the most famous tattoo artist in the world' by Vogue, elevating tattoo artistry in celebrity and fashion circles.

notable_figures.name: Maud Wagner
notable_figures.contributions: First known female tattoo artist in the United States, breaking gender barriers in the early 20th century.
notable_figures.influence: Pioneered women's participation in tattooing, paving the way for future female artists.

notable_figures.name: Samuel O'Reilly
notable_figures.contributions: Patented the first electric tattoo machine in 1891, revolutionizing the craft.
notable_figures.influence: His invention enabled more detailed and efficient tattooing, fundamentally changing the industry.

notable_figures.name: Ramon Sokun
notable_figures.specialty: Realism with Southeast Asian art influences
notable_figures.contributions: Specializes in Cambodian and broader Southeast Asian motifs, preserving cultural heritage through tattooing.
notable_figures.influence: Dedicated to infusing ancient Southeast Asian art into contemporary tattooing, pushing creative boundaries.

notable_figures.name: Gabrielle Widjaja
notable_figures.specialty: Chinese cultural artifacts, porcelain motifs, floral patterns
notable_figures.contributions: Reclaiming and celebrating Asian heritage within the tattoo community, especially in queer and diaspora contexts.
notable_figures.influence: Significant in promoting cultural authenticity and community connection in tattooing.

notable_figures.name: Jakoh
notable_figures.specialty: Traditional Japanese Irezumi with Southeast Asian influences
notable_figures.contributions: Trained under Master Horitatsu, blending authentic Japanese techniques with regional motifs.
notable_figures.influence: Gained prominence in the global tattoo scene by blending cultural influences.

notable_figures.name: Hotbirdbath (之) Lu
notable_figures.specialty: Surreal, folkloric designs inspired by Chinese and Southeast Asian folk art
notable_figures.contributions: Creates designs incorporating mystical animals and deities, emphasizing body autonomy and cultural roots.
notable_figures.influence: Their work serves as therapeutic and cultural expressions, particularly within queer and diasporic communities.
